newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU URGES POLAND, HUNGARY TO MAKE EXTRA EFFORTS.
newsitem.headline: EU URGES POLAND, HUNGARY TO MAKE EXTRA EFFORTS.

text.p: The European Union told two of the eastern European countries expected to be first in line to join early next century they had to make further efforts to avoid unnecessary delays in crossing the threshold.
EU foreign ministers told counterparts from Poland and Hungary that while their national EU integration strategies were on the right track for EU membership, they had to run even faster.
"The Union hopes that the follow-up in terms of sectoral strategy will offer a clear plan for implementation," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo said of the Polish efforts.

EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said after the meeting with Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati that extra efforts were needed in areas stretching from agriculture through regional policy, to banking and privatisation.

An EU position paper prepared for the meeting with Poland said "the Union expects the Polish authorities to give priority to this task in such a way as not to delay the moment when Poland will be ready to join."
The EU position on Hungary said "a lot still remains to be done to fully adopt (EU legislation) and to ensure its implementation."
It pointed to areas like regional policy and privatisation where Hungary could pull up its socks.

At the meetings, held annually to review trade and other ties under association accords, Poland and the EU settled a number of trade rows, including one over citrus fruit which earlier this week threatened to derail the meeting.
Poland agreed to bring into line a value added tax on imported citrus fruits which Spain said amounted to protectionism.
Poland and the EU also ended disputes over car assembly regulations in Poland, Polish recognition of European Union product certificates and an understanding on Poland's fuels sector.
"We have responded to and suggested what we intend to do.... which is considered by the Union as the correct approach," Rosati told the news conference.

Poland and Hungary, along with the Czech Republic, are seen as the countries most likely to cross the EU threshold first. The European Commission is currently finalising individual reports on 10 central and eastern European countries which have applied to join the bloc.
The others are Slovenia, Slovakia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Romania.
The advice is expected to be unveiled by the EU executive on July 15, after which EU government will take their decision on which to open talks with. REUTER
